column2: The tribunes of the Communard Cities have gathered in Magritta, and for once they agree on something. Our cities have traded on the southern seas for longer than anyone remembers, yet every year newer merchants crowd into our waters: Tilean upstarts, Arabyan corsairs and the guildsmen of the north. They want to know what the High Tribune means to do about it.
Buy up the trading posts along the southern coasts.
Trade can wait. Arm the cities.
The Marienburg League is the real rival. Take them on.
Each Communard house with the coin to spare buys a trading post on the coasts of Estalia, Tilea, Araby or the Badlands, paying its old owner.
The Communards seize one of the Marienburg League's trading posts, and the two merchant powers become bitter rivals.
The Communard Concord

The Communard Cities of Estalia have bound themselves in a new Concord. Their houses are buying trading posts all along the southern coasts, and they pay in good silver, which makes them hard to refuse. The old masters of the southern seas mean to stay its masters.
The Communard Cities of Estalia have bound themselves in a new Concord, and its first act was to arm every guild and street. Whoever means to take the old free cities will find them ready.

The Communard Cities of Estalia have bound themselves in a new Concord and declared the Marienburg League their rival. Communard ships have already taken one of the League's trading posts. The two greatest merchant powers of the Old World are at each other's throats.
Interesting.
The Concord stands.
An agent of one of the Communard houses has bought our trading post. Their offer was too generous to refuse, and they made it clear that the next one would not be.
At least we were paid.
Communard ships have sailed into one of our trading posts, run up their colours and told our factors to leave. The Concord means to break the Marienburg League's hold on the seas.
They will regret this.
Communard Free Ports
The Communard houses are buying trading posts all along the southern coasts.
Communard City Militias
Every guild and street of the Communard Cities has been armed.
Rival of the Marienburg League
The Communard Concord is fighting the Marienburg League for the trade of the seas.

Pigbarter stands on great silt pillars above the River Ruin, where the river spills its poisons into the Scalded Delta and a yellow, acrid smoke hangs over everything. It is the end of the Ivory Road and home to five houses from five corners of the world: an Arabyan house from Copher, a Westerlander one from Marienburg, a Cathayan one, a Reman one and a Strigany one. Gnoblars swarm in the shantytown below, ogres and greenskins roam the hills, and the houses have agreed to share the cost of keeping their town alive. They want to know where the money should go.
Keep the eagle-owls flying over the rooftops.
Put the coin into the pig-joust. Friends are cheaper than walls.

Pigbarter is under attack, and word has gone out along the trade roads. The houses' kin in Copher, Marienburg, Remas, Sylvania and far Cathay have answered with what merchants know best: a ship has come in heavy with gold.
Blood is thicker than trade. Mostly.

It is time for the pig-joust again, the event Pigbarter is named for. Merchants, gamblers, ogre maneaters and greenskin chiefs are already crowding the walkways, and the pens are full of snorting war-pigs. How the Trademaster spends the day will be remembered across the delta.
Host it lavishly and invite the neighbours.
Run the betting tables.
Ride a pig myself!
Gnoblars from the shantytown under the stilts have been climbing up at night, tearing themselves on the glass and nails along the roof edges and still making off with half a warehouse of goods.
The eagle-owls will see to them.
Hang the ones we catch from the rooftops.
Pay them to leave the warehouses alone.

Woodworm, centipedes and lice have eaten deep into the timbers that hold Pigbarter above the river. A whole row of houses sagged into the shantytown last night, and the gnoblars below were delighted. The engineers say the pillars must be shored up, at a price.
Pay to shore up the pillars.
It has stood this long.
A caravan has come in off the Ivory Road, its ogre guards half-starved and its wagons heavy with silk, jade, spices and stranger things. Every house in Pigbarter wants a piece of it.
Pigbarter takes its cut.
The Fall of Pigbarter

Pigbarter has fallen. The stilt town over the River Ruin could not hold out against its neighbours forever, and its merchant houses have gone home: the Arabyans to Copher, the Westerlanders to Marienburg, the Remans to Remas, the Strigany to Sylvania, and the Cathayans back along the Ivory Road to Cathay. There will be no more pig-jousts on the delta.
A pity. It was good for trade.
Stilt Town of the Scalded Delta
Pigbarter stands on silt pillars over the poisoned River Ruin. Its roofs are edged with broken glass and nails, and no army camps long in the toxic delta around it.
Eagle-Owls of Pigbarter
Trained giant eagle-owls patrol the skies over Pigbarter and hunt down gnoblar raiders.
Rotting Stilts
Woodworm and lice are eating the timbers that hold Pigbarter up, and parts of the town have collapsed into the shantytown below.
Trampled by a War-Pig
